steps: Parts laid out. Press Assemble, or drag the timeline. Cut away slices the case open through its front posts.
The power bank drops into the tray, ports at the open end and display facing the window in the far wall. The spring fingers behind it and beside it flex back and pin it in place.
The rail plate slides in from the front until its barbs click into the slots in the tray walls.

The Pi drops onto four tapered pins that rise from the case floor through its mounting holes. Each pin stands on a post, and each post sits on a strip of floor cut free so it can flex like a diving board.
Four printed spacers drop onto the pin tips poking up through the Pi. They replace the HAT kit’s brass standoffs and screws.
With the ribbon plugged into the Pi, the HAT drops onto the spacers’ own pins. The ribbon runs under the HAT and up through its slot to the HAT’s connector.
The case slides onto the offset rails until the latch post clicks into its notch. It only fits one way round.
The fan pushes up into the collar under the lid, and its two clips catch it.
Tilted, the lid’s skirt hooks into the groove on the outside of the USB-end wall; then it swings down. Its four posts land on the HAT’s corners and push the stack 0.4 mm onto the sprung floor strips.

The key slides in through both long walls and the two lugs under the lid, and clicks home flush. Now the lid can’t lift, even in a drop. To open: push the key out from the cable side with a pen, swing the lid up, unhook it.
